newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo government sources deny dinar to be devalued.
newsitem.headline: Yugo government sources deny dinar to be devalued.

text.p: Yugoslav government experts on Monday denied rumours of a pending devaluation prompted by the appearance of a new 100-dinar banknote, launched last week to ease day-to-day payments.

The street market reacted to the new banknotes with a dinar slide to 3.6-3.7 to the German mark after the currency idled at 3.5 for weeks. Some traders said it had to do with more dinars in circulation in general.
"There are plenty of dinars around. The government has paid out pensions, wages to teachers and the dinar fell," a black market dealer told Reuters.
The dinar is officially fixed at 3.3 to the German mark. It was last devalued by 70 percent in November 1995 after being fixed at par to the mark since January 1994.
Economists said there were no economic reasons for the dinar to depreciate now that the country received a fresh hard currency boost from its recent $1 billion Telekom's sale.

"There is absolutely no reason to devalue. It would be a suicide to do such a thing ahead of the (Serbian) elections. The dinar will remain stable until September at least," a senior government, official who declined to be named, told Reuters. -- Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
